newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Tuesday.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Tuesday morning a 40-billion-bolivar ($83 million) auction of 178-day VE6MTMAoRR "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills, with a 16.89 percent coupon.

The bank said it would also offer 10 billion bolivars ($20.75 million) in 267-day bills VE9MTMAoRR with a 17.24 percent coupon and another 10 billion bolivars of 351-day bills VE1YTMAoRR with a 17.58 coupon.

Coupons at the Tuesday auction, brough forward one day because of May 1 Labour Day holiday, are up from last week's 60-billion bolivar issue. Then 178-, 267- and 358-day notes carried 16.09, 16.41 and 16.74 percent coupons respectively for effective yields of 16.89, 18.31 and 19.47 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
